newsitem.title: UK: Ireland warns UK against Sellafield nuclear dump.
newsitem.headline: Ireland warns UK against Sellafield nuclear dump.

text.p: The Irish government warned Britain on Monday that it would fight plans to build an underground nuclear dump near Sellafield, which backs onto the Irish Sea and said it would explore the "legal options" open to Ireland to block the move.

Emmet Stagg, minister of state for Ireland's department for transport, energy and communications, made the comments at a press briefing in London as part of a visit to raise the profile of opposition to the so-called NIREX proposal. Sellafield is a nuclear complex, based in Cumbria, north west England.
"The reason I have decided to come to London is to highlight the Irish government's concerns following a further submission made by me to the UK authorities," he said.
The Irish minister added that the "environmental threat of a nuclear waste dump so near to the Irish Sea warranted such intenvention."
He added that unless resolved, NIREX could become "The potential source of dispute between our two countries.'

When asked what Ireland would do if Britain pushed ahead with plans for the dump, he said "We will examine the options legally open to us." He said the Irish government's attorney general was exploring such possibilities at present.

NIREX was recently refused planning permission by the Cumbria County Council. Emmet said it already had evidence of minor accidents occuring and was worried about the impact of a major incident on Ireland as well as the UK.
"If small accidents can occur on a regular basis, we are feaful a major accident could occur," he said.
